key_facts: July 28 UPDATE (Reuters/Straits Times, Al Jazeera, Arab News, Khaleej Times July 28 + 2 Exa searches): Still NO official announcement of a new multinational maritime coalition through July 28. However, Riyadh's centrality tightened further on July 28: (1) Houthis fired ballistic missiles at another Saudi oil tanker in the Red Sea (UKMTO confirmed explosion), stepping up their blockade on Saudi shipping; (2) GCC foreign ministers held a video call Tuesday July 28 discussing intensifying cooperation on freedom and safety of vessels; (3) Saudi Crown Prince MBS held talks with new UK PM Andy Burnham specifically condemning Houthi threats to Red Sea navigation; (4) Yemeni FM-designate Afrah al-Zouba warned from Riyadh of Houthis copying Iran's Hormuz model; (5) China held quiet bilateral talks with Houthis solely to clear Chinese tankers individually; (6) US-Iran pause entered day 4 with Trump focused on Oman-mediated Hormuz talks rather than announcing a new US-led Red Sea coalition. Adjusted Saudi Arabia 0.56->0.58, Egypt 0.12->0.13, United Kingdom 0.04->0.05, trimming United States 0.15->0.12, France 0.06->0.05 (sum 0.93).
